messages:
emma: Heads up — customer reported 400s when using pagination examples for /v1/list-files. Docs show `cursor: 0` and `page_size: 50` in examples, implying numeric cursor. Runtime expects an opaque cursor string token (e.g. 'eyJhbGci...'). Their retry logic increments cursor as number and breaks.

josh: Yikes. Which snippets use the numeric cursor?

emma: Node + curl examples under docs/snippets/list-files.openapi.md and examples/list-files.md. Also the OpenAPI example schema has `cursor: integer` which is wrong.

priya: I can fix the OpenAPI schema to make cursor a string and update examples to show opaque token and guidance: "cursor is an opaque token; do not parse or increment." Also add migration note advising to replace numeric handling with token passthrough.

josh: Please also add a validation test in docs CI to ensure example payload types match the OpenAPI schema so this doesn't slip again.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 by priya changes: openapi schema cursor type -> string, updated Node/curl examples, added migration note. CI: docs-lint passed.

emma: Customer confirmed that switching to token passthrough fixed their integration. They had been incrementing cursor as a number, causing malformed requests.

priya: I'll land the PR and add a short bullet in the changelog: "Pagination cursor is opaque string — do not treat as numeric offset." Also adding an FAQ entry under docs/faq/pagination.md.

josh: Good. Can you include a tiny code snippet showing how to safely handle pagination in Node: store cursor as string, call until cursor is null/empty.

priya: Yep — example: `while(cursor){ const res = await client.listFiles({cursor, page_size:50}); cursor = res.meta?.next_cursor || null; }`

docs-bot: PR merged to main: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789. Staging docs rebuilt.

emma: Thanks — marking this resolved for the customer. Will reopen if anything else pops up.
